Watts made this hymn from Psalm 12, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Help, O LORD, for the godly are no more; the faithful have vanished from among men. 2They lie to one another; they speak with flattering lips and a double heart. 3May the LORD cut off all flattering lips and every boastful tongue. 4They say, “With our tongues we will prevail. We own our lips—who can be our master?” … 4 more verses PSALM 12 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 12
But lips, that with deceit abound, Shall not maintain their triumph long; The God of vengeance will confound The flattering and blaspheming tongue. STANZA III
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 1. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
